'''Dmitrii Konstantinovich Faddeev''' ({{lang-rus|Дми́трий Константи́нович Фадде́ев||ˈdmʲitrʲɪj kənstɐnʲˈtʲinəvʲɪtɕ fɐˈdʲe(j)ɪf}}; 30 June 1907 – 20 October 1989) was a Soviet mathematician known for his work in algebra, number theory, homological algebra, computational mathematics, and mathematics education. He is also recognized for one of the earliest axiomatizations of [[Shannon entropy]] in probability theory.<ref name="Fad1">{{cite journal |last1=Aleksandrov |first1=A. D. |last2=Bashmakov |first2=M. I. |last3=Borevich |first3=Z. I. |last4=Kublanovskaya |first4=V. N. |last5=Nikulin |first5=M. S. |last6=Skopin |first6=A. I. |last7=Yakovlev |first7=A. V. |title=Dmitrii Konstantinovich Faddeev (on his eightieth birthday) |journal=[[Russian Mathematical Surveys]] |date=1989 |volume=44 |issue=3 |pages=223–231 |doi=10.1070/RM1989v044n03ABEH002126 |translator-first=A. |translator-last=Lofthouse |url=https://www.mathsoc.spb.ru/pantheon/faddeev/UMN-89e.html |via=[[Saint Petersburg Mathematical Society]] |publisher=[[Russian Academy of Sciences]] |s2cid=250913337 |issn=0042-1316|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Dmitrii Konstantinovich Faddeev - Biography |url=https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Biographies/Faddeev/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250615204704/https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Biographies/Faddeev/ |archive-date=2025-06-15 |access-date=2025-10-21 |website=Maths History |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref name="Fad2">{{cite journal |last1=Borevich |first1=Z. I. |last2=Linnik |first2=Yu. V. |last3=Skopin |first3=A. I. |title=Дмитрий Константинович Фаддеев (к шестидесятилетию со дня рождения) |journal=Russian Mathematical Surveys |date=1968 |volume=23 |issue=3 |pages=169–175 |doi=10.1070/RM1968v023n03ABEH003777 |trans-title=Dmitrii Konstantinovich Faddeev (on his sixtieth birthday) |publisher=[[Russian Academy of Sciences]] |s2cid=250895230 |language=ru |issn=0042-1316}}</ref>

==Biography==
Faddeev was born on 30 June 1907 about 200 kilometres south-west of Moscow, on his father's estate. His father, Konstantin Tikhonovich Faddeev, was an engineer, and his mother was a physician with a deep interest in music that inspired Dmitrii's lifelong love of the piano. Friends later recalled his musical talent as both expressive and entertaining.<ref name=":0" />

He graduated from [[Saint Petersburg State University|Leningrad State University]] (then Petrograd State University) in 1928, where his teachers included [[Ivan Matveyevich Vinogradov]] and [[Boris Delone|Boris Nicolaevich Delone]]. In the mid-1920s he also studied at the composition department of the Leningrad Conservatory, but did not complete that course. In 1930 he married [[Vera Faddeeva|Vera Nicolaevna Zamyatina]] (Faddeeva), with whom he later co-authored works in numerical analysis. They had three children, including the mathematical physicist [[Ludvig Faddeev]] ({{lang-rus|Фаддеев Людвиг Дмитриевич||fɐˈdʲe(j)ɪf ˈlʲudvʲɪk dmʲˈitrʲɪjɪvʲɪt͡ɕ }}).<ref name=":0" />

From 1934 he worked at the [[Academy of Sciences of the Soviet Union|Mathematical Institute of the Academy of Sciences of the USSR]], and from 1940 at the [[Steklov Institute of Mathematics|Leningrad Branch of the V. A. Steklov Mathematical Institute]], where he headed the Laboratory of Algebra. He became a professor at Leningrad State University in 1944 and served as Dean of the Faculty of Mathematics and Mechanics from 1952 to 1954. For many years he chaired the Department of Algebra and later directed the Mathematics Division of the faculty.

==Scientific work==
Faddeev's research spanned ''number theory'', ''algebra'', ''homology in groups'', and ''computational mathematics''. In algebra, his main focus was the [[inverse Galois problem]] — the search for algebraic extensions with a prescribed Galois group over a given field. He also obtained results in homological algebra and in applied mathematics worked on linear-algebraic algorithms, notably the [[Faddeev-LeVerrier algorithm]] for computing the adjugate matrix and characteristic polynomial.

In [[probability theory]], he authored an early paper "On the concept of entropy of a finite probabilistic scheme".<ref name=":1"/> In this note Faddeev gave a three-axiom characterization of [[Shannon entropy|Shannon's entropy]] based on continuity, symmetry, and recursive additivity. These axioms simplified the earlier system of axioms proposed by [[Aleksandr Khinchin]] (1953)<ref name=":2">{{Cite journal |last=Khinchin |first=A. Ya. |date=1953 |title=The concept of entropy in the theory of probability |journal=Uspekhi Matematicheskikh Nauk |volume=8 |issue=3(55) |pages=3–20 |trans-quote=English translation in ''[[Russian Mathematical Surveys]]'' vol.~8, no.~3 (1953), pp.~3--20}}</ref> and later played a role in [[information theory]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Khinchin |first=A. I. |date=1934 |title=Zur axiomatik der Theorie der Information |journal=A Theory of Language and Information |volume=1 |pages=17–46 |trans-quote=English translation: ''A Mathematical Theory of Information'', Dover, 1957}}</ref><ref name=":2" /><ref name=":1">{{Cite journal |last=D. K. Faddeev |first=D.K. |date=1956 |title=On the concept of entropy of a finite probabilistic scheme |journal=Успехи Математических Наук(Uspekhi Matematicheskikh Nauk) |volume=11 |issue=227–231 |pages=227–231 |trans-quote=English translation in ''AMS Translations'', Series 2}}</ref>

Together with [[Vera Faddeeva]] he wrote ''Numerical Methods in Linear Algebra'' (1960; enlarged edition 1963). For instance, they developed an idea of [[Urbain Leverrier]] to produce an algorithm to find the [[resolvent formalism|resolvent matrix]] <math>(A - sI)^{-1}</math> of a given matrix ''A''. By iteration, the method computed the [[adjugate matrix]] and [[characteristic polynomial]] for A.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Hou |first1=Shui-Hung |date=January 1998 |title=Classroom Note:A Simple Proof of the Leverrier--Faddeev Characteristic Polynomial Algorithm |journal=[[SIAM Review]] |publisher=[[SIAM|Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]] |volume=40 |issue=3 |pages=706–709 |bibcode=1998SIAMR..40..706H |doi=10.1137/S003614459732076X |issn=1095-7200}}</ref> With I. S. Sominsky he co-authored ''Problems in Higher Algebra'', which was translated into several languages.

==Educational work==
Since the 1930s he organized and conducted school [[mathematical olympiad]]s and built a strong pedagogical community in Leningrad. He was one of the founders of Boarding School No. 45 for Physics and Mathematics (now the [[D. K. Faddeev Academic Gymnasium]] of [[Saint Petersburg State University]]).<ref name="Sokolova40">{{cite news |last1=Sokolova |first1=N. N. |date=16 October 2003 |title=К 40-летию физико-математической и химико-биологической школы-интерната №45 при ЛГУ |url=http://old.journal.spbu.ru/2003/22/9.shtml |agency=Saint Petersburg University}}</ref> From February 1965 he served as its scientific curator and later as a member of the school council.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://agym.spbu.ru/en/history |title=D. K. Faddeev Academic Gymnasium History |publisher=Saint Petersburg State University}}</ref>

==Students==
Faddeev's students included [[Mark Bashmakov]] <small>([[:ru:Башмаков, Марк Иванович|ru]])</small>, [[Zenon Borevich]], [[Lyudmyla Nazarova]], [[Andrei Roiter]], [[Alexander Skopin]], and [[Anatoly Yakovlev]] <small>([[:ru:Яковлев, Анатолий Владимирович|ru]])</small>.<ref name=":0" />
